- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Martha Kahn [6. Juli 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.145
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.145
- Datum: 6.7.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
7 Ramapo Road,
Ossining, N.Y.
6.7.41.
Dear Marta,
I often think of you and of the year we spent
together in Bath, but now more than ever because we are
again in a house for the summer, after a too long time
of hotel- and restaurant life. There is some similarity to
Mrs Leckie's house as regards position, but neither house
nor landscape are to be compared with Bath although
Ossining is rather pretty. There are no walks round here
and nothing is to be seen - unless you have a car and go
for rides along pretty roads. I am trying to find someone
with whom I can go out in a car, get some practice and
knowledge of the traffic rules and then take my driving test
again to be ready if one day we should decide to live in
the country for longer. For although a bus passes near here
one is lost without a car as most people live away from
bus or railroad lines. I was able to take over the maid with
the house and that simplified everything, of course. She can
cook meats and vegetables and is willing to do more but
any kind of desert which does not come out of a tin or is not
made just by adding water to some ready-made mixture, is
quite unknown to her. But this does not matter very much.
I shall try to pass on to her what I myself still dimly
remembers of the art of cooking and there is in the house a
book with recipes. In any case we enjoy very much being
out in the country. There is a nice lawn round the house
it is about as secluded from the road as Mrs Leckie's house,
there is a porch for Stefan to work on he need not dress and
I can go even to the village in slacks. Two other advantages
are that we are near Eva and not even an hour from New
York. It is not much cooler than New York in day time, but the
air is nice and if it smells, it smells of flowers and grass.
Today we have Eva with us and to-morrow I shall go with her
to New York and return her to Croton on Tuesday. We would
have liked to keep her longer but there is really nothing
whatsoever for her to do here except to read. I hear that you are
always busy and at least not lonely. But it seems strange that
Love is now in Bath and that you may not be there. Life certainly plays
unexpected tricks on us nowadays, and God knows where we will be in
3 or 6 months time. Anyway, we had that year in Bath which I thoroughly
enjoyed and I have the good feeling that you too felt at home in Rosemont.
Kindest regards to all, yours,
Lotte.

Kindest regards and love from Stefan
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Lotte Zweig. Die Zeilen am linken Rand wurden nachträglich von Stefan Zweig hinzugefügt. Sehr gut lesbar.
Rückseite des Dokuments, leer (durchscheinender Text der Vorderseite erkennbar).
